When it comes to skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed products, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Caire Beauty reflects demand for hormone-aware skincare for women aged 40 to 65-plus, offering science-driven formulas designed to address the visible effects of perimenopause and menopause through advanced hydration and skin-rebuilding technologies.

Love From Yours highlights the rise of AI-powered personalized skincare, using skin analysis and lifestyle data to create customized routines tailored to individual needs. Radical Skincare represents continued interest in clinical-strength anti-aging solutions that deliver restorative results while remaining suitable for sensitive and blemish-prone skin. Scarlett Whitening, an Indonesian brand, signals growing demand for accessible, ingredient-focused skincare that combines brightening, hydrating, and acne-targeting actives.

On TikTok, #GlutenFreeMakeup reflects growing interest in inclusive beauty products that cater to ingredient-conscious consumers and specific lifestyle preferences. #FrenchTwistHairstyle and #ColorMelting reflect growing interest in elevated yet wearable hair looks, with consumers embracing timeless styling techniques alongside dimensional, natural-looking hair color trends. #CreamyEyeliner highlights demand for versatile eye makeup products that offer smooth application, rich pigmentation, and effortless wear. #MorningMakeupRoutine points to consumers seeking efficient, everyday beauty rituals and product recommendations that simplify their routines. Together, these trends reflect growing demand for beauty solutions that balance self-expression, convenience, and performance.

In the haircare space, there is growing interest in haircare solutions that combine convenience and science-backed ingredients alongside targeted treatments to support hair and scalp health. Convenience is a big factor, with waterless dry shampoo and 6-in-1 shampoo signaling the desire for multifunctional products that simplify hair care routines.

Caffeine hair serum highlights increasing interest in scalp-focused formulations designed to help strengthen hair, reduce shedding, and promote the appearance of fuller, healthier-looking hair. Exosome hair therapy underscores the growing popularity of advanced, science-driven hair restoration technologies, with consumers exploring treatments aimed at supporting scalp health, hair regeneration, and overall hair vitality. Finally, overnight hair serum reflects rising demand for treatments that work while users sleep, delivering deep hydration, nourishment, and repair to improve hair strength and smoothness by morning.

These trends can also been seen across the haircare brands spiking interest, with science and ingredients sitting at the forefront. Hair fall, thinning hair and scalp health are key concerns, with Minimalist and South Korean brand Aromatica showing up as trending haircare brands. Iso Beauty highlights interest in haircare solutions that deliver salon-quality results at home, while &Honey underscores the popularity of Japanese hair care brands with formulations inspired by honey-based ingredients catering to consumers seeking hydration, shine, and frizz control. Meanwhile, Wow Skin Science reflects continued demand for plant-based haircare products.

On TikTok, #BadNailsCheck has users showing manicure disasters, sharing nail art that turned out completely different from the reference photo. In contrast, #DamagedHairSolutions signals users on a “healthy hair journey”, sharing tips, routines, and product recommendations for repairing damaged hair. #DIYBlush reflects the growing appeal of personalized beauty, with creators customizing blush shades. #MotherOfTheBrideMakeup highlights demand for elegant, age-inclusive makeup inspiration for weddings and other special occasions. Meanwhile, technicians and creators are sharing techniques, product recommendations, and behind-the-scenes glimpses of their daily work with #LashArtistOfTikTok.

In the wellness space, there’s a growing interest in supplements and solutions that support long-term health, targeted nutrition, and proactive selfcare. Dopamine patches align with demand for wearable wellness solutions aimed at supporting focus, motivation, mood, and cognitive performance. The rise of menopause support supplements highlights interest in formulations that help manage hormonal changes, with consumers seeking products that address symptoms such as hot flashes, mood fluctuations, sleep quality, and overall wellbeing.

Meanwhile, kimchi supplements mirror continued focus on gut health, as more consumers look for probiotic-rich alternatives inspired by fermented foods to support digestion and microbiome balance. Vitamin B5 supplements lean into essential nutrients that aid the breakdown of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, while supporting skin and heart health. Finally, longevity supplements satisfy a growing focus on healthy aging, with consumers seeking science-backed ingredients and formulations that support cellular health and vitality as part of a preventive approach to wellness.

When it comes to wellness brands, those spanning targeted delivery formats, science-backed nutrition, and performance-focused solutions are performing the best. Gentle Patch reflects demand for convenient, wearable wellness solutions, while Bioschwartz and Webber Naturals represent continued interest in supplement brands that offer vitamins, minerals, probiotics, and herbal formulations for everyday health. Swolverine signals growing demand for performance nutrition that supports strength and recovery, while Zhou Nutrition reflects interest in holistic supplements that promote energy, immune health, sleep, and healthy aging.

On TikTok, the #SummerGlowMakeup and #BeautyFavs hashtags reflect growing interest in curated beauty routines and product discovery, with consumers seeking seasonal makeup inspiration alongside trusted product recommendations. #GeodeNails lean into a demand for artistic, statement-making nail designs that emphasize creativity and self-expression. #DIYMicroLocsJourney adopts a personal storytelling format, as consumers document their hair journeys, while learning protective hair styling techniques. Meanwhile, #DollarTreeSkincareHaul spotlights affordable skincare products, as consumers explore budget-friendly options that fit into their selfcare routines.

In the bodycare category, there’s growing interest in products that combine targeted treatments, ingredient-focused formulations, and at-home wellness solutions. The rise in searches for cellulite oil suggests that consumers are seeking botanical oil blends and firming formulations designed for massaging into the skin as part of anti-cellulite routines. Grape soap highlights demand for playful, fruit-inspired products that combine functionality with novelty and aesthetic appeal. Meanwhile, the popularity of AHA body lotions signals continued interest in ingredient-led skincare, with consumers seeking exfoliating body creams that improve skin texture and smoothness. Epsom salt lotion and red light therapy panels reflect the growing adoption of at-home recovery and wellness routines, as consumers seek products and devices that support muscle comfort, recovery, skin rejuvenation, and temporary pain relief.

Science-backed brands with plant-based ingredients and luxury positionings are soaring. Hada Labo, a Japanese brand, and QV Skincare reflect continued demand for gentle, hydration-focused products that support healthy skin through barrier-supportive formulations. Just Nutritive signals a consumer preference for handcrafted, botanical-based products that emphasize naturally derived ingredients, while Nordic Goddess points to the growing intersection of wellness and bodycare, as more consumers seek topical solutions that incorporate THC and CBD for targeted relief. Meanwhile, La Mer underscores demand for premium bodycare, combining intensive hydration with a luxurious, sensorial experience.

Over on TikTok, #CheetahHair, #HaircutTutorials, and #HairFoils are all trending, reflecting a broader shift toward more experimental and technique-driven approaches to hair styling. #CheetahHair highlights bold, pattern-led hair looks that emphasize self-expression and visual impact, #HaircutTutorials points to the growing demand for accessible, step-by-step education from hair stylists, while #HairFoils underscores continued interest in professional coloring techniques. In addition, #PlaitsBraids highlights the appeal of finished braided styles, with content featuring both at-home and salon-created results for men and women. Meanwhile, #CoconutOilForSkin signals an ongoing interest in multi-purpose ingredients used across selfcare routines. Together, these trends reflect a move toward both skill-based hair experimentation and ingredient-driven selfcare practices.

Luxury fragrances are becoming more than a special occasion spritz. Consumers are investing in scents that have wide appeal, from sport fragrances for energy, freshness, and an active lifestyle, to sweet smells that have a touch of nostalgia.

Tomato perfume underscores the rise of unconventional fragrance notes, reflecting curiosity around earthy and garden-fresh scent experiences that stand apart from traditional or gourmand offerings. Meanwhile, perfume-making kits are becoming increasingly popular, as rising interest in personalization and creativity push consumers to explore DIY fragrance creation and craft scents tailored to their individual preferences.

Riiffs and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect growing consumer demand for accessible fragrances with strong, long-lasting effects and scent profiles that blend Middle Eastern perfumery traditions with modern styles. Pure Instinct and Rahasya signal interest in fragrances that feel more personal and body-driven, where consumers are drawn to scents designed to interact with individual chemistry and enhance perceived personal appeal. Lore reflects demand for more experiential and concept-led fragrances, as consumers increasingly seek scents that go beyond smell to evoke places, moods, and narratives. Meanwhile, Miu Miu highlights the enduring influence of fashion houses within the fragrance category, as consumers continue to seek scents that blend luxury, creativity, and modern self-expression.

#RedDyedHair, #LashDye, and #SelfTannerHack all reflect a broader shift toward at-home beauty experimentation through DIY techniques. #RedDyedHair highlights bold self-applied color changes as a form of personal expression and transformation. #LashDye reflects interest in low-maintenance beauty routines, where users tint lashes for longer-lasting definition, and #SelfTannerHack shows how shared tips are used to achieve more controlled, even tanning results. Then, #NosePatches and #NeckSkincareRoutine point to growing demand for targeted skincare solutions, with the former focusing on pore care and blackheads for a quick, temporary smoothing effect, while the latter underscores increasing awareness of often-neglected areas that require attention beyond the face. Together, these trends reflect a move into DIY-driven beauty and targeted treatment routines.

When it comes to nails, consumers are seeking designs that blend self-expression, practicality, and care. BB cream nails reflect demand for natural-looking, low-maintenance manicures, while comic nails highlight a desire for creative and expressive nail art. Matcha nails point to the growing traction of soft green tones, influenced by the cult popularity of the beverage, while solid gel nail glue indicates interest in durable, mess-free nail application, as consumers increasingly value long-lasting performance. Crystal nail files reflect a growing awareness of nail health, with consumers seeking gentler tools that help maintain strong, smooth nails and minimize damage.

The rise of The Gelbottle, Nail Reformation, Kleo Kolor, and Curvlife each proves growing demand for long-lasting nail solutions that deliver salon-quality results. The Gelbottle reflects interest in professional-grade systems that strengthen and enhance natural nails, while Nail Reformation and Kleo Kolor point to the popularity of reusable press-ons and durable at-home manicure options. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light. Meanwhile, Hermès underscores the premiumization of the nail category, with consumers seeking luxury nail products and tools featuring shades inspired by Hermès’s design heritage and silk draping — finished with a high-gloss, satin sheen in a single coat.

On TikTok, #CyberPunkNails reflects interest in futuristic nail art that combines punk influences, neon accents, metallic finishes, and bold 3D details. #SkinTintStick highlights demand for hybrid complexion products that offer light coverage with skincare benefits in a portable format. #TCAPeel and #MicrobiomeSkincare signal growing consumer interest in understanding the mechanisms behind skin behavior, from chemical exfoliation and skin renewal to the role of the microbiome in barrier health. In the case of #TCAPeel, viral social media content often emphasizes the risks of extreme at-home use. #HairLossJourney extends this same behavior pattern into haircare, where individuals actively seek to understand the causes of hair loss, sharing progress and seeking support and solutions. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward beauty that combines experimentation, care, and awareness of underlying skin and hair health.

Makeup products and techniques that deliver precision, convenience, and natural-looking results are soaring. Contour stain reflects demand for long-wearing, transfer-resistant sculpting products that provide definition with minimal maintenance throughout the day. Meanwhile, cool-toned blush and cool-toned contour underscore consumers’ increasing focus on shade accuracy. At the same time, ghost and pre-glued lashes highlight demand for effortless lash enhancement, combining natural-looking results with faster and easier application methods. Together, these trends suggest that makeup is evolving toward personalized routines that prioritize subtle enhancement, ease of use, and products tailored to individual features and preferences.

Across makeup brands, the rise of Elroel and Purito highlights the continued influence of K-beauty. Elroel reflects growing demand for adaptive complexion products that simplify shade matching, while purito emphasizes lightweight coverage and minimal formulations to avoid skin sensitivities. Dermatologist-founded Rodan and Fields further reinforces interest in hybrid complexion products that combine cosmetic performance with skincare benefits. Meanwhile, the popularity of Brow Daddy highlights consumers’ focus on expertly defined brows and professional-grade beauty solutions offering precision and long-lasting results. KJH.Brand, launched by makeup artist Katie Jane Hughes, underscores the appeal of creative, multi-use makeup that encourages self-expression and flexible application across the eyes, lips, and cheeks.

As more consumers focus on maintaining hair health and reducing damage, #BedtimeHaircare is trending on TikTok and reflects growing interest in overnight prevention treatments. #CollagenFilm highlights K-beauty innovation in the form of dissolvable collagen films, designed for topical application to deliver instant hydration and a smoother, firmer appearance. #BrowFreeze, meanwhile, reflects continued interest in lifted, feathered brow styling that creates a laminated look. #613AmazonWig signals demand for affordable, pre-lightened platinum blonde wigs that enable bold color experimentation without chemical processing, while #GluelessClosureInstall reflects a broader shift in wig culture toward accessible, low-damage styling, where consumers seek dramatic transformations that are easy to apply, comfortable to wear, and avoid the long-term commitment or potential damage associated with traditional installation methods. Together, these trends reflect a move to beauty routines that balance care and transformation, combining preventative habits with low-damage styling and skin-focused innovation.

Consumers are on the hunt for science-led skincare innovations. Interest in silicone scar sticks reflects demand for effective scar products that support skin recovery and improve the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, while simplifying daily treatment routines. Rising interest in needle patches highlights demand for advanced delivery technologies, which enable active ingredients to be delivered directly for enhanced efficacy and targeted results. PDRN creams and serums tap into regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas associated with skin repair, recovery, and renewal. Meanwhile, growth in matte lip balms highlights a desire for hybrid lip products that bridge skincare and makeup, delivering hydration while providing both a tint and a matte finish.

Among trending skincare brands, Elm Biosciences underscores the rise in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a lab-to-patient approach focused on supporting long-term skin health and healthy aging. Wow Skin Science reflects demand for nature-inspired skincare, offering plant-powered formulations free from harsh chemicals. Sincerely Yours highlights the rise of dermatologist-developed skincare tailored to younger consumers, with a focus on barrier support and the unique needs of teenage skin. Isispharma represents the continued strength of dermocosmetic skincare, providing targeted solutions for concerns such as hyperpigmentation, rosacea, and acne through dermatologist-recommended formulations. Sunplay signals growing emphasis on daily sun protection, leveraging advanced Japanese skincare technology to deliver high-performance UV defense.

On TikTok, #FireHair reflects growing interest in bold, high-impact hair color trends, as more consumers embrace expressive styles. #DyedLocsOnWomen highlights demand for dyed locs as a form of color expression across textured and protective hairstyles. #ShimmerLips leans into the continued interest in glossy, light-reflecting lip finishes, while #WrinkleTreatments underscores rising focus on preventive and corrective skincare solutions, as consumers seek ways to address aging. #HDFrontalWigs showcases high-definition lace frontal wigs, with content centered on installations and styling.

In the haircare space, consumers are searching for products that combine active ingredients, scalp support, and at-home technology. Amino acid shampoos and Capixyl-based formulas reflect a demand for ingredient-led repair and solutions that strengthen hair, while addressing thinning and scalp health. Batana oil shampoos highlight an ongoing interest in nourishing botanical ingredients for hydration and scalpcare, while blonde hair masks emphasize maintenance of tone and softness in color-treated locks. At the same time, red light therapy hats signal the growing adoption of tech-enabled tools for scalp stimulation and hair growth.

Hairburst reflects a growing demand for haircare solutions that support stronger, longer hair and address thinning and breakage. KilgourMD represents a dermatologist-founded, science-backed approach to scalp health, offering a targeted system designed to treat hair thinning through plant-based prevention and care. Tgideas highlights interest in rosemary-based botanical haircare aimed at supporting growth, reducing breakage, and improving scalp health. Dr. Groot reflects the strength of Korean dermatological haircare that zeroes in on scalp balance and hair loss prevention through ingredients such as niacinamide, prebiotics, and probiotics. Trybello signals demand for haircare solutions designed to reduce hair loss and promote thicker, fuller-looking hair.

On TikTok, #HeatlessStyling reflects rising interest in low-damage hair routines, as consumers seek ways to achieve results without heat tools. #FastHairstyles highlights demand for quick, efficient styling solutions that slot into busy lifestyles while still delivering polished looks. #FaceGlitter signals continued engagement with expressive makeup, focused on bold, playful self-expression. #MonsterHighNails points to the rise of bold, character-inspired nail designs that emphasize individuality and playful aesthetics, especially among Gen Alpha consumers. #NailArtBrush points to the importance of precision tools in nail design, supporting detailed artwork and professional techniques, alongside guidance from nail techs on choosing the best brushes and how to use them effectively.

Consumers are increasingly drawn to wellness formats that blend supplementation, wearables, and at-home recovery tools into everyday routines. Pheromone gummies reflect growing interest in products that support confidence with a holistic appeal, while dopamine patches align with demand for wearable solutions aimed at focus, motivation, and cognitive performance. GLP-1 and NAD+ patches support metabolism, energy, and cellular function, and multi-collagen supplements continue to gain traction for beauty and structural benefits such as skin, hair, and joint health. Alongside these, percussive massage devices highlight the rise of accessible recovery technologies designed to reduce muscle tension and support circulation after exercise. Together, these trends reflect a shift toward personalized wellness routines using multiple formats that prioritize convenience and seamless integration into everyday life.

Javvy Coffee reflects growing demand for functional beverages that integrate wellness benefits such as supporting energy. Myvitamins focuses on simple, accessible nutrition through a wide range of vitamins and supplements that support general health and daily wellbeing. Esther Formula is a South Korean supplement brand known for its glutathione direct films and reflects the rising demand of K-wellness along with beauty-from-within nutrition, where consumers prioritize skin health and radiance through targeted supplementation, along with interest in innovative delivery formats. Swolverine represents performance-focused supplementation designed to support strength, endurance, and recovery through clinically dosed products. Jacob reflects demand for high-protein functional foods made from simple, real ingredients.

#DIYMakeupHacks highlights growing interest in at-home beauty experimentation and resourceful routines, as consumers share and test creative ways to achieve makeup results. #DIYBlush reflects personalization in beauty, with users exploring custom or handmade blush products to tailor color and finish. #SunscreenPowder points to demand for convenience and reapplication-friendly sun protection formats that support on-the-go skincare routines. #NailAcrylic signals focus on durability and design in nailcare, as users compare acrylic applications for strength, longevity, and aesthetic results. #MicroLocInstall reflects interest in protective hairstyling and long-term hair maintenance, particularly around the installation and upkeep of microlocs. Together, these trends show a shift toward DIY beauty, convenience, maintenance-focused routines across makeup, skincare, nails, and haircare.

In bodycare, current search trends reveal a strong focus on targeted skin benefits and functional treatment-based products. Epsom salt lotions reflect an interest in convenient options for muscle relief and recovery. Grape soap highlights playful, fruit-inspired formats and visually appealing hand soaps designed to resemble grapes, pointing to a rise in products combining functionality with novelty and aesthetic appeal. Moroccan black soap indicates a keen interest in deep cleansing and exfoliation rooted in traditional formulations. Kojic acid lotions are part of a continued attention to skin brightening and evening tone. Meanwhile, the growth of glass foot files reflects a preference for reusable at-home tools that effectively smooth and exfoliate.

As for brands, Papatui reflects a growing interest in the men’s bodycare space, which combines approachable grooming routines with skin-focused formulations, as well as strong demand for its tattoo care line in collaboration with Dwayne Johnson. Luv Scrub, meanwhile, signals a rising demand for authentic African mesh body exfoliators, designed to cleanse and smooth the skin, inspired by traditional West African bath rituals. GoPure Beauty is a results-driven bodycare brand centered on accessible firming and brightening solutions, while QV Skincare offers sensitive-skin solutions rooted in dermatologist-backed, barrier-supportive formulations designed for everyday use. Cyklar highlights the rise of fragrance-forward bodycare that merges fine fragrance inspiration with sustainable practices and sensorial personal care experiences.

This week, #WashAndSet reflects a continued interest in professional salon services on TikTok, where hair is washed, conditioned, and set on rollers before drying to create smooth, polished, and long-lasting results. #CherryAngioma signals the growing consumer attention toward skin education and concerns, as users seek information around specific skin conditions. The #LashExpert hashtag points to demand for specialized beauty professionals who showcase precision techniques and lash transformations, while #MakeupWithSPF captures the rising interest in hybrid beauty products that combine cosmetic performance with everyday sun protection. #StylistHair signals engagement with hairstylist-driven content that blends transformations and recommendations from experts. These trends reveal that beauty consumers are increasingly drawn to content centered on expert guidance, visible results, and multifunctional routines.

There’s a growing interest in more personalized and occasion-driven fragrance choices. The search for masculine fragrance suggests that scent is increasingly functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Indie perfume highlights a shift toward niche artistry and unique scents. Birthday cake perfume points to playful, gourmand fragrances inspired by dessert-like notes. Bridal perfume underscores the role of scent in key life moments, with consumers seeking signature fragrances for special occasions. Meanwhile, clean fresh perfume indicates that consumers continue to seek out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to richer, gourmand scents.

Arabiyat Prestige and Assaf, both Arabian fragrance houses, reflect a growing interest in heritage-led scents defined by richness, high concentration, and long-lasting wear. YCZ signals the rise of social media-driven accessibility, where viral scents and dupes offer more affordable alternatives to traditional designer perfumes. Tenth Muse reflects interest in solid perfumes that prioritize portability, skin sensitivity, and easy application. Sorce underscores interest in bold, imaginative fragrances that lean into gourmand and whimsical scent profiles inspired by fantasy and more playful notes.

On TikTok, #PrismHair reflects an interest in bold, color-driven hair looks that emphasize a multi-tonal, iridescent finish. #NaturalNailJourney highlights a shift toward nail health and growth, as consumers document and prioritize stronger, natural nails. #KeratinOil points to demand for ingredient-led care for the scalp and beard, focusing on smoothing, repairing, and enhancing shine. #BridalMakeupArtists captures both final results and day-to-day content, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the work and routines of bridal artists. #MillennialSkincare signals continued engagement from this generation, as they share routines that balance efficacy, prevention, and maintenance in skincare. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing aesthetic expression with long-term care and behind-the-scenes visibility across beauty content.

Nail trends are getting personal, with consumers adding letters to their nails or intricate patterns like gingham. Other styles that are popular in search are matcha nails, leaning into soft green tones, influenced by the cultural clout of the beverage. The rise of nail art tools signal growing interest in the techniques behind these looks, as consumers aim to create more complex designs. Together, these trends indicate that the nail category is evolving toward more creative and customizable expression, blending personal style, technique, and design.

Diamond Cosmetics highlights demand for affordable, everyday tools, making essential nail utensils widely accessible. Nail Reformation reflects interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails that offer a salon-level, damage-free alternative to shellac. Kleo Kolor focuses on durable, at-home manicure systems, including gel press-ons and LED gel strips designed for long-lasting wear. The Gel Bottle has released variations of pigments, foils, and brushes that enable the creation of more intricate nail art. Curvlife emphasizes ease of application through reusable soft gel press-ons and adhesive solutions that don’t require UV light, while Onyx Professional, with products like Hard As Hoof, points to a preference for treatment-focused nailcare that strengthens and repairs weak or brittle nails.

On beauty TikTok, #OrangeCandle reflects interest in DIY hacks that show how to make a candle from an orange using simple household items, creating a citrusy aroma. #BlackGirlWashDay highlights routine-focused care tailored to textured hair, emphasizing maintenance and health. #PermRodSetNaturalHair points to technique-driven styling for defined, heat-free curls. #WingedLinerTutorial underscores demand for step-by-step guidance in achieving precise makeup looks, while #LongHairHack signals interest in tips and shortcuts for managing and styling long hair. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking practical, how-to guidance across routines, techniques, and hacks in beauty content.

Current search data reveals a growing interest in functional, personalized makeup. Interest in lip volumizers reflects a demand for hybrid lip products that combine hydration, smoothing, and visible plumping with a high-shine finish. Lipstick printers, associated primarily with YSL, signal curiosity around tech-enabled customization, enabling personalized shades on-demand. Gluten-free lipstick highlights rising awareness of ingredient sensitivities, while medium-coverage concealer points to a preference for balanced, skin-like finishes. Meanwhile, the rise of cool-toned blush underscores a want for precise shade matching, as consumers seek out colors that better complement their undertones. Together, these trends indicate that makeup is evolving toward customized, results-driven routines that combine performance, personalization, and ingredient-conscious choices.

The rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes. Caia Cosmetics highlights a demand for accessible, high-quality makeup that delivers an effortless, glowing look similar to Jung Saem Mool, which leans into a Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Rodan + Fields signals an interest in hybrid complexion products combining coverage with skincare benefits. Overall, makeup is evolving toward accessible, glow-focused, and treatment-infused routines that blend professional performance with everyday wearability.

On TikTok, the rise of #LocDetoxing reflects a demand for deep-cleansing routines that support scalp and hair health, particularly among protective styles. #HairPlop highlights an interest in techniques that enhance natural texture, especially for defining curls with minimal effort. #TakingDownBraids points to maintenance-focused content, as consumers navigate the full lifecycle of protective styles. #SunscreenApplication underscores growing attention to proper usage and technique in daily skincare routines, while #AirbrushSprayTan focuses on in-process guidance, from what to wear to how to ensure even results. Together, these hashtags show that consumers are seeking guidance across application and maintenance in beauty content.

In skincare, current search data reveals a rising focus on advanced, treatment-led products. Interest in scar sticks reflects demand for targeted solutions that simplify care for specific concerns. PDRN cream and serum signal growing awareness of regenerative ingredients, as consumers seek formulas tied to skin repair and renewal. Exosome serum highlights increasing interest in next-generation, science-backed actives, while high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) underscores the influence of non-invasive, clinic-inspired technologies, as consumers look for lifting and firming benefits beyond topical products. Together, these trends indicate that skincare is evolving toward highly targeted, science-driven routines that blend efficacy, innovation, and treatment-level results.

ELM Biosciences underscores the growing interest in science-backed, clinically developed skincare, with a “lab-to-patient” approach supporting long-term skin health and the concept of aging well. AO Skincare signals demand for antioxidant-rich formulas that strengthen skin resilience against environmental stressors. Organic Apoteke reflects continued interest in holistic, ayurvedic-inspired skincare, as consumers seek gentle solutions for concerns like acne and sensitivity. Yepoda Skincare and Tosowoong, both Korean brands, highlight the influence of active-led formulations and high-concentration products targeting concerns such as acne, pigmentation, and aging.

On TikTok, #MicroLinksHairExtensions are trending, reflecting demand for natural-looking length and volume, as consumers invest in seamless hair enhancements. #ViralDollarTreeMakeup highlights budget-conscious beauty discovery, with users testing affordable products. #HairWashDays points to routine-driven content, as consumers build and share structured care rituals for healthier hair. #PlumperLips underscores ongoing interest in enhancement-focused beauty, whether through techniques or product-driven results, while #MomHairHack spans both child hair solutions and quick, practical styling for moms themselves. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, affordability, and routine-friendly approaches to beauty content.

Current search data reveals a haircare consumer increasingly focused on targeted, treatment-led products. Interest in protein-free shampoo reflects demand for gentler formulations tailored to specific hair needs, particularly for those avoiding protein overload. Amino acid shampoo signals a shift toward ingredient-led repair, as consumers seek formulas that strengthen and support hair health. Dry shampoo paste highlights demand for multi-functional refresh solutions that absorb oil and add texture. Meanwhile, overnight hair serum shows growing interest in treatments that work during sleep, delivering hydration, repair, and frizz reduction without requiring extra time in the morning routine, and red light therapy hats underscore the rising adoption of tech-enabled solutions for scalp health and hair growth. Together, these trends indicate that haircare is evolving toward personalized, treatment-driven routines that combine efficacy, convenience, and innovation.

Playa Beauty reflects interest in California-inspired products promising effortless “beach hair”, supporting minimalist routines while enhancing natural waves and movement. California Baby underscores demand for gentle, plant-based products suitable for babies, children, and adults with sensitive skin. Ducray points to a growing appetite for clinically backed, condition-specific solutions, offering dermatologically tested treatments for dandruff, hair loss, and sensitive scalps. Dr. Groot, a Korean brand, highlights a consumer focus on scalp health and anti-hair loss solutions. Indian-inspired ayurvedic haircare brand Champo uses ingredients such as myrobalan fruit extract, gum arabic, and geranium oil to resonate with a consumer seeking easy packaged haircare, rather than performing weekly ayurvedic hair oiling. California Naturals signals interest in natural, nourishing formulas that strengthen hair.

On TikTok, #DitchedTheDye reflects a shift among older women embracing their natural hair color and moving away from maintenance-heavy routines. #ILoveCurlyHair highlights a growing appreciation for natural texture, as consumers celebrate and care for their curls. #PromMakeupInspo points to planning and inspiration for key events, with users seeking polished, occasion-ready looks. #CubanTwistHair underscores interest in protective styling and cultural hair practices, while #HairFoam signals demand for styling products that enhance texture and hold. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing self-expression, hair health, and event-driven styling in beauty content.

Consumers are increasingly seeking convenient, easy-to-use formats and wearable solutions for functional wellness, with patches offering targeted support for mood, metabolism and cellular health. Dopamine patches target focus and cognitive performance, while GLP-1 and NAD patches support metabolism, energy and cellular function. Cutting Jelly reflects interest in supplements for weight management and fat reduction and pressotherapy points to growing demand for non-invasive recovery and circulation-boosting treatments. These trends show wellness routines evolving beyond basic supplementation toward a focus on energy to fat reduction and enhanced circulation.

Javvy Coffee reflects growing interest in functional beverages that combine everyday rituals with wellness benefits, offering convenient ways to support energy and focus. A1 Supplements and MTS Nutrition underscore demand for performance-driven sports nutrition, including muscle building, bodybuilding and post-workout recovery, appealing to consumers seeking results-oriented solutions. Lullabites points to a desire for wellness products that support rest and recovery, emphasizing functional snacks designed for relaxation and sleep. IM8 Health, co-founded by David Beckham, highlights interest in simplified, all-in-one nutrition that combines multiple supplements into a single, convenient daily drink. What’s That Patch is delivering patches packed with nutrients that help with sleep, stress, productivity and more. Together, these brands reveal that wellness consumers are seeking products that are functional, evidence-based and seamlessly integrated into daily routines.

#LashGlues highlights interest in product performance and comparison between brands, as consumers test glues for reliable, long-lasting lash applications. #MakeupSamples reflects budget-conscious discovery, with shoppers exploring trial sizes and low-commitment ways to test products. #HairTrial points to planning and preparation, as users test styles ahead of key moments. Meanwhile, #HerbalHairGrowthOil signals demand for natural, treatment-focused solutions, and #BushyBrows spans interest from managing and shaping fuller brows to enhancing volume and testing products. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing performance, planning and creativity in beauty content.

There’s an increasing focus on functional, treatment-led bodycare products that deliver targeted results. Interest in epsom salt lotions reflects a demand for convenient, topical solutions that soothe sore muscles and support recovery. Searches for kojic acid lotions and turmeric body washes signal a growing focus on brightening and tone correction across the body, as consumers turn to ingredient-led solutions that address hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone. Silicone loofahs and glass foot files point to a preference for hygienic, durable tools that elevate cleansing and exfoliation, while addressing concerns around bacteria and skin safety.

The rise of Crowned Skin reflects a shift toward multifunctional bodycare, as well as an interest in products like body butter colognes, which combine deep hydration with long-lasting fragrance. Bepanthol highlights demand for clinically backed, multi-purpose solutions that protect and regenerate sensitive or compromised skin. Vermont Soap underscores an interest in gentle, non-irritating cleansers and bar soaps that replace harsher detergents, reflecting a move toward safer, skin-friendly formulations. Meanwhile, Luna Daily and Kate McLeod point to growing desire for specialized and ritualized bodycare — from microbiome-balancing formulas safe for all areas of the body, to waterless, solid moisturizers that emphasize sustainability and sensorial experience.

#CheapBeauty is trending on TikTok, showing that consumers are exploring budget-conscious cosmetic options and highlighting an interest in affordable products. #SkincareComedy reflects engagement with humorous, relatable beauty moments, where audiences enjoy playful takes on everyday experiences. #HairExtensionInstallation points to professional, technique-focused content, as viewers watch skilled stylists demonstrate expert application and installation. Meanwhile, #SkinTighteningTreatment and #VolumeWispy capture aspirational results, from creams that enhance skin firmness to professional lash services that create full, wispy volume, proving that beauty audiences remain captivated by visible, high-impact transformations. Together, these trends show that consumers are balancing entertainment, affordability, and aspirational transformations across beauty content.

There’s a craving for gourmand fragrances taking place, as rich, edible-inspired scents capture consumer attention. Searches for masculine fragrances suggest that scent is functioning as an identity marker for male consumers, driving greater interest in variety and personalization. Tomato perfume reflects curiosity around hyper-specific, ingredient-led scents that invite consumers to reimagine familiar smells in a new context. Solid fragrances, meanwhile, point to demand for portable alternatives to spray bottles, where fragrance layering can extend beyond the home. Finally, clean, fresh perfumes reveal how consumers are seeking out fresh, lighter options as a counterpoint to rich, gourmand notes.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a consumer shift toward heritage-rich fragrances known for their high-concentration and long-lasting power. YCZ captures the rise of social media-driven accessibility, proving that viral scents can provide high-quality alternatives to designer perfumes at an affordable price point. Narcotica underscores the appeal of the niche Italian market, where the focus is on “addictive”, high-concentration gourmands that blend bold sweetness with luxurious, long-lasting ingredients.

#TrippyNails are trending, showing that consumers are drawn to surreal, psychedelic nail aesthetics that use distorted patterns and holographic finishes to create eye-catching results. #EasterMakeup reflects a fascination with seasonal, pastel-driven makeup, highlighting how soft color palettes and whimsical details capture attention during spring celebrations. #MakeupCleansingBalm points to growing interest in high-performance cleansers that remove heavy makeup without drying out the skin or leaving it feeling stripped. Meanwhile, #GRWMDate and #HairGoneWrong capture unfiltered, relatable beauty experiences. The former centers on personal storytelling and dating life while getting ready, and the latter highlights the reality of styling mishaps, illustrating how beauty audiences value both the social side of getting ready and the more candid moments that happen along the way.

What’s drawing consumers in? According to data, its playful and creative nail expressions. There’s increased interest in stained glass and matcha nails, as users seek visually striking, color-rich designs that combine artistry with trend-driven aesthetics. Meanwhile, polka dot nails highlight a preference for playful patterns that add personality to everyday manicures. The rise of nail art pens signals a move toward precision and customization. Finally, solid gel nail glue indicates attention to durable, reliable application, showing that consumers value long-lasting performance alongside unique nail looks.

In terms of brands, the rise of Heyhae reflects a shift toward convenient, at-home nail solutions, as more consumers value semi-cured gel strips, which can be applied under natural sunlight for quick, non-toxic manicures. Diamond Cosmetics highlights the demand for affordable, everyday nail tools, making professional-grade manicures accessible to a wide audience. Nail Reformation demonstrates interest in high-quality, reusable press-on nails, offering a salon-level, damage-free experience at home. Meanwhile, Sunuv and IBD Beauty underscore the appeal of salon-level equipment and innovations — from UV and LED lamps to builder gel.

This week on TikTok, #RobeCurls are trending, as more consumers are drawn to heatless styling techniques that simplify hair routines while delivering defined, natural-looking results. #IceCreamNails reflects a fascination with playful, dessert-inspired nail aesthetics, which underscore how novelty textures and creative color palettes capture attention across nail content. The #LipOilGloss hashtag spotlights lip products that combine shine, nourishment, and a lightweight feel in everyday routines. Meanwhile, #SoftBridalMakeup and #GenZMakeup captures two parallel beauty directions: one centered on polished, natural elegance for milestone events, and the other revealing side-by-side contrasts between Gen Z and millennial makeup styles. Together, these trends show how consumers are balancing practical beauty solutions, playful visual trends, and cross-generational style influences.

Subtle, natural-looking makeup continues to be popularized by medium-coverage products such as concealers. The rise of cool-toned blush and illuminating drops further signals a move toward color theory-informed customization, where consumers use specific undertones and light-reflecting finishes to create a healthy and natural glow. There’s also demand for clean mascara, where lightweight, ingredient-conscious formulas are favored. Another trend on the rise is gluten-free lipsticks, pointing to growing attention to health-conscious formulations.

The rise of Tilt Beauty reflects a shift toward accessible, inclusive design, showing that consumers value products tailored to different abilities and needs. Jolie Beauty highlights the demand for alternative, high-performance makeup that allows bold self-expression while remaining vegan and cruelty-free. Skindinavia demonstrates a preference for long-lasting, professional-grade finishes, while Jung Saem Mool underscores the appeal of luxury Korean expertise that delivers natural, glowing skin. Meanwhile, Concrete Minerals signals a move toward transparent formulations with bold pigments, as shoppers increasingly prioritize ingredient-conscious choices.

#RushedMakeup shows that consumers are drawn to quick, ready-to-go routines that demonstrate how to look polished fast. #NailTechASMR reflects fascination with sensory content. #BeforeAndAfterFacelift signals that audiences are intrigued by dramatic visual transformations of cosmetic procedures. #SisterLockRetightening and #WigLaid highlights a strong interest in professional hair care expertise and the maintenance of intricate, high-effort hairstyles, while also capturing attention to precision and seamless style by showcasing how flawlessly wigs are styled and finished.

The rise of scar sticks, PDRN serums, and liquid microneedling reflects a consumer increasingly invested in skin regeneration, barrier repair, and clinically backed ingredients. The portability and ease of scar sticks signal demand for convenient, targeted solutions, while liquid microneedling highlights appetite for professional-level collagen stimulation and enhanced absorption without in-clinic procedures. Growing interest in milk sunscreens signals demand for high-performance UV protection that feels lightweight, skincare-forward, and multifunctional. There’s also growth in matte lip balms, with Celine launching refillable matte lip balms accompanied by a special installation at Harrods on March 2.

Trending skincare brands reflect a shift toward clinically grounded, barrier-focused skin health paired with sustainability and device-led innovation. Genabelle and Tosowoong, both K-beauty brands, exemplify this movement: Genabelle develops science-backed, microbiome and PDRN-driven formulas designed to repair the skin barrier, while Tosowoong targets brightening, anti-aging, acne, and dehydration. At the same time, the growing attention around Shark’s CryoGlow LED mask, targeting acne, fine lines and puffiness, reflects a desire for professional-grade treatments that accelerate results, reduce inflammation, and replicate clinic-grade procedures. Meanwhile, Bolt Beauty’s biodegradable single-dose capsules and Yepoda’s K-beauty-inspired active formulations underscore the rising ingredient literacy of consumers.

On TikTok, the #FlawlessBraids hashtag is largely driven by hair stylists showcasing intricate braiding techniques, alongside AI-generated concepts of futuristic braiding devices that don’t yet exist — but imagine faster styling without sacrificing precision. Meanwhile, #NeonHairColor highlights bold experimentation and personal expression, while #GlowSunscreen reflects a skin-first mindset where protection and radiance are expected to work hand in hand. #ShadowLiner signals interest in detailed, technique-focused eye artistry, as creators break down application methods for more defined eye looks. #LipEssentials points to demand for streamlined, everyday lipcare that balances performance with convenience.

The surge in beauty tools like red light therapy hats suggests that consumers are increasingly seeing the scalp as the biological foundation of hair quality, density, and longevity, embracing device-led, clinically inspired solutions they can use conveniently at home. Interest in ingredient-specific shampoo formulas featuring batana oil and amino acid, or those that are protein-free, reflects a more educated haircare buyer. Meanwhile, demand for hair smoothing serums points to a parallel desire for immediate polish and manageability. Together, these trends reveal a consumer who approaches haircare through targeted, science-backed and ingredient-conscious solutions.

Seapuri and Dr. Groot, both Korean brands, tap into the rising demand for scalp-focused, anti-hair loss care. Seapuri uses hydrating, mineral-rich formulas, including a water-based scalp serum to reduce hair loss and balance sebum, while Dr. Groot focuses on scalp-nourishing shampoos and targeted anti-hair loss solutions with a clinically inspired, results-driven approach. LED brands like CurrentBody, Shark, Solawave, Vym, Monastery and FAQ have also been leading the charge. Roz sits at the intersection of plant-based sustainability and professional performance delivering botanical-powered results that promote lasting scalp health. This positioning bridges the gap between the accessible, plant-based approach of California Naturals and the salon-quality focus of ISO Beauty — underscoring how consumers increasingly seek conscious formulations alongside visible, high-performance results.

On TikTok, hashtags like #BraiderOfTikTok and #BridalGlamLook are largely driven by professionals showcasing intricate techniques and polished transformations, suggesting that users turn to the platform for inspiration. Meanwhile, #TryingNewHairstyles highlights a culture of experimentation and style switch-ups, while #SkincareMasks documents selfcare routines as part of an ongoing beauty journey. #RedHeadMascara points to growing demand for hyper-specific, shade-inclusive products, revealing that consumers are actively searching for solutions tailored to their unique features.

There’s a growing interest in topical, bioactive wellness formats, with patches incorporating GLP-1s and NAD reflecting a shift to skin-applied solutions for metabolic support, longevity, and targeted physiological optimization. At the same time, consumers are searching for supplements such as oregano oil and L-theanine powder, pointing to continued demand for immune resilience and stress management through more traditional, scientifically informed formats. Cutting jelly, a Korean wellness supplement, is gaining traction for its appetite-suppressing, digestion-supporting, and fat-management proposition. Its popularity highlights a broader preference for convenient, flavorful, and results-driven wellness rituals. Collectively, these trends reflect a consumer mindset that blends experimentation with intentionality, seeking measurable benefits through both topical innovation and functional nutrition.

The latest search trends show that consumers are treating wellness as a seamless part of daily life rather than a task. By brand, Javvy Coffee reflects a desire to turn everyday rituals into functional routines that boost physical performance, while Wellah signals interest in precise, results-driven nutrition for recovery and hydration. Lullabites points to a focus on restorative sleep supporting energy and clarity for the day ahead. Crisp Power highlights the rise of indulgent snacks that also meet fitness goals, and Magic Spoon shows that nostalgic, enjoyable foods are increasingly expected to deliver health benefits without compromising taste.

On TikTok, hashtags like #PinkAndPurpleHair and #PersonalizedFragrance are driven by users embracing beauty as a form of self-expression and creativity, from bold hair colors and custom scents to playful hair accessories like bows. Trends such as #LipLinerPencil highlight a desire to explore colors and combinations for defined, polished looks. Meanwhile, content around #RetentionTips indicated that beauty consumers value expert guidance and skillful maintenance, ensuring they get the most out of specialized treatments such as lash extensions.

Consumers are going beyond basic hygiene in search of specialized products, like Epsom salt lotions for muscle recovery. The rising interest in PH-balanced body washes and fungal infection lotions highlights a shift toward dermatological wellness. At the same time, tools like the glass foot file are gaining traction, reflecting a consumer focus on at-home pedicures and skin maintenance. Meanwhile, the demand for Moroccan black soap underscores a desire for ‘heritage efficacy’, where users seek out natural, ritual-based exfoliation to minimize synthetic chemical alternatives. These trends signal a more literate consumer who views the entire body — not just the face — as a landscape for clinical, preventative, and holistic care.

The rising search interest in brands like GoPure Beauty, QV Skincare, Diptyque, Susanne Kaufmann, and Bliss reflects a consumer shift toward the skinification of the body, whereby users demand high-performance active ingredients for use beyond their face. This behavior indicates a shift to clinical wellness, with shoppers balancing a need for dermatological efficacy and targeted solutions with a desire for the sensory luxury and ‘clean’ prestige offered by Diptyque and Susanne Kaufmann.

On TikTok, content featuring hashtags like #HairExtensionInstallation and #BrowThreading are dominated by professionals sharing techniques, as more consumers use the platform to get inspiration or find services. In contrast, #MixedHairstyles and #HairExtensionsHack are mostly driven by users exploring practical options and DIY approaches to at-home styling. Elsewhere, #CrueltyFreeCosmetics reflect a growing interest in ethical and sustainable products, showing that conscious choices are increasingly part of beauty conversations online.

The rise in sweet fragrance searches shows consumers are craving comfort and indulgence. Interest in tomato perfume and milk fragrances points to a growing appetite for unconventional, nostalgic aromas that blur the line between food and scent. The emergence of edible perfume — designed to be safely consumed — signals a shift toward playful, multisensory experiences in which application extends scent beyond the skin. Meanwhile, demand for white floral perfume suggests that classic, elegant profiles continue to anchor consumer preferences amid experimentation.

The popularity of Middle Eastern houses like Arabiyat Prestige, Gulf Orchid, and Assaf highlights a shift toward luxurious and statement-making scents. Assaf, in particular, offers luxurious, often unisex fragrances that combine oud and incense with contemporary, international notes. The rise of Xinu, meanwhile, points to a growing interest in artisanal storytelling and plant-based ingredients. Also on the rise is XO Khloé, underscoring the continued power of celebrity-led fragrance lines.

The rise of #PinkNailDesign and #BraidsAndBows highlights playful, creative styles, while #GenZMakeup favors fresh-faced, natural looks with fun touches like graphic eyeliner, pastels, and faux freckles. The growth in #JLoMakeup is being driven by Jennifer Lopez’s Golden Globes look, which was inspired by the early-aughts supermodel glam that users are eager to recreate. The growth of #FirstTimeBotox signals increasing openness and transparency around cosmetic procedures, as users frame treatments as relatable milestones rather than taboo transformations. Meanwhile, #HoneyHairMask highlights a parallel interest in plant-based, at‑home haircare rituals focused on nourishment and maintenance.

Consumers are going for self‑expression, playful motifs and hybrid styles when it comes to nail art. Searches for cat eye heart nails, pink cat eye nails, and cat claw nails show that consumers are blending shape‑driven trends with tactile finishes, embracing looks that feel both edgy and whimsical. Meanwhile, strawberry shortcake nails point to a nostalgia‑infused trend. The interest in Cynthia Erivo nails highlights how celebrity‑inspired nail looks can drive demand, with users translating red carpet or character‑driven aesthetics into their own manicure repertoire.

The top‑growing nail brands reflect a consumer shift toward at‑home expertise and expressive finishes. Heyhae’s popularity signals a desire for playful, design-forward polishes and tutorials that help users translate looks for everyday wear. Gaoy and Rossi Nails underscore the rise of DIY gel systems and professional‑grade kits, revealing that consumers seek salon‑quality results at home. Jodsone’s ascent points to a craving for art‑centric, niche lacquer brands that stand out with unique color stories. Meanwhile, IBD Beauty highlights continued demand for reliable, performance‑driven products in the professional and enthusiast space, especially among gels and long‑wear finishes.

On TikTok, trending beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that blends identity‑driven aesthetics, routine conservation and sensory‑led selfcare. The popularity of #PastelGothMakeup shows how users are embracing expressive beauty looks, using makeup as a form of cultural and creative identity. Hashtags like #SkincareRestock and #ShampooRoutine points to the importance of consistency and ritual. #StrawberryScents highlights an interest in nostalgic fragrance profiles, while #BasketballHairstyle reflects the influence of purpose‑driven, activity‑ready beauty content.

Consumers are getting creative thanks to the popularity of peel-off lip tints and liners. The rise of blue lip stain, which applies blue but reveals a pink or berry hue once peeled, speaks to the demand for color-shifting, pH-reactive formulas that feel personalized and surprising. Plumping lip liner reflects a desire for makeup that mimics cosmetic procedures, with consumers drawn to products that visibly enhance lip volume without injections. Meanwhile, plum mascara shows how consumers are exploring non-traditional but wearable color accents.

The top-growing makeup brands reveal a consumer shift toward inclusive design, minimalist aesthetics, as well as age and tool-specific solutions. Tilt Beauty reflects rising demand for accessible, user-friendly packaging and refillable formats that are sustainable. Sweed Beauty appeals to a growing audience seeking the no-makeup makeup look, through vegan formulations that deliver barely-there finishes for natural enhancement over heavy coverage. Maange shows that consumers are investing in quality makeup brushes and application tools, signaling increased interest in the techniques behind the look, not just the formulas themselves. Meanwhile, Jung Saem Mool attracts those drawn to editorial-inspired, K-beauty artistry, and Prime Prometics caters to the needs of mature skin, emphasizing that makeup shoppers are increasingly seeking products that serve their specific life stage and texture needs.

The rise of #HairExtensionsTutorial and #TakingOutBraids shows that users are actively seeking step‑by‑step guidance for maintenance and technique. #FrenchHairPin and #PurpleHairDye underscore a growing appetite for aesthetic experimentation and trend‑inspired looks, where tools and color become playful ways to express personal style. Meanwhile, #UltaHairSalon points to the influence of in‑salon experiences and professional authority in shaping consumer choices, with users looking to bridge DIY learning and expert execution.

Skincare products that blend restorative care, gentle technology and everyday indulgence are on the rise. The popularity of scar sticks and PDRN serums points to the advancement in regenerative treatments that support healing and skin repair. Tools like ultrasonic skin scrubbers highlight consumers’ appetite for at‑home derm‑tech devices. Also, melting lip balms and pore care are trending as consumers seek results‑driven everyday products.

Brands with ingredients-conscious efficacy, modernized wellness and at-home performance solutions are being sought after. Terra Lotus, powered by beef tallow-based care, signals a growing interest in animal-derived, nutrient-dense skincare rooted in traditional practices, as consumers seek richer, bioavailable alternatives to plant oils and lab-created moisturizers.

APLB and Genabelle continue to spike interest in science-backed K-beauty, especially products targeting hydration, brightening, and skin regeneration through actives like niacinamide and glutathione. Dermagist points to sustained interest in cosmeceutical-style anti-aging solutions. Finally, Shark Beauty’s expansion into skincare devices reflects the growing appeal of tech-enhanced and at-home treatments.

Consumers are eager to participate in viral beauty without overspending, as #AffordableLipOil and #AffordableMascara make strong cases for accessible versions of trendy, functional products. #ProfessionalHairProducts point to a growing appetite for salon-quality care. In contrast, #HydroDermabrasion reflects a rising interest for in-spa skincare treatments, as consumers turn to TikTok to understand the benefits of medical-grade exfoliation and glow-boosting facials. Meanwhile, #CranberryMakeup underscores the continued influence of seasonal and mood-based beauty aesthetics, as users experiment with rich, warm tones to express personal style.

Exfoliating foot masks and hand masks are on a spike, as consumers approach the treatments with the same ritualistic care traditionally given to the face. Vegan body wash and magnesium body butter reflect a shift toward wellness‑aligned, ingredient‑conscious products. Meanwhile, exfoliating body lotion bridges treatment and care, showing the consumer’s need for multifunctional products that improve texture and moisture in a single step.

Kate McLeod and Brown Sugar Babe offer sensory bodycare experiences, from exfoliating stones to whipped butters. Brands like Dettol and Noshinku show that trusted hygiene and germ‑defense solutions remain top of mind. Bend Soap Company’s artisanal approach highlights the appeal of small‑batch, craft formulations.

These top‑growing TikTok beauty hashtags reveal a consumer mindset that values efficacy, personalization, real‑world practicality and community‑driven discovery. The popularity of #ScienceBasedSkincare and #SkincareApp shows that users are increasingly seeking data‑informed products and digital tools. At the same time, #LazyGirlSkincare and #ThinHairTips reflect a demand for simple, low‑effort solutions that fit into busy lifestyles or specific concerns. On the makeup side, #BlushLovers highlights the enduring appeal of color cosmetics.

The surge in interest for marshmallow perfume and chocolate perfume reflects a continuous craving for gourmand, dessert‑inspired scents. The rise of rose vanilla perfume and bridal perfume suggests people are gravitating toward romantic and memory‑evoking fragrances. Growing searches for oil‑based perfume show an increased interest in long‑lasting and body‑centric scent formats, revealing a preference for fragrance that melds seamlessly with one’s natural scent and lasts longer than traditional sprays.

Matière Première takes on the farm‑to‑fragrance purity and minimalist luxury, with its raw material‑focused compositions. La Sultane de Saba Paris channels consumer interest with olfactory-inspired notes. Similarly, The Maker Perfume hints at a growing demand for identity‑driven scent choices over mass market fragrances. Meanwhile, legacy and designer‑adjacent brands like Hugo Boss and Penhaligon’s continue to draw attention for their heritage and status, even as they explore niche alternatives.

Sensitivity-aware routines, personal customization and ingredients‑led problem-solving beauty are growing hashtags on TikTok.

The popularity of #SensitiveSkincare shows more people are seeking gentle, irritation‑free formulas. Meanwhile, #UnderratedSkincare suggests a hunger for hidden gems or under-the-radar products, meaning consumers are increasingly willing to explore beyond mainstream brands. The rise of #BlondeHighlightsOnDarkHair and #HairLoss captures demand for hair‑specific solutions and transformation content, as users look for guidance and community advice on challenging hair goals. Finally, #CoffeeSkincare points to the ongoing appeal of natural, functional ingredients, as people are drawn to the antioxidant and circulation‑boosting benefits of coffee in skin and hair routines.

Bold nails are back and it’s all about self‑expression and textured innovation with growing interest in statement cheetah print designs rooted in nostalgia and glamour, blending animal prints with modern finishes and clever color shifts. The appetite for animalistic styles continues with cat eye nails reflecting excitement around method‑driven finishes — using magnetic polish to create shimmering dimension that feels both futuristic and accessible. Water drop nails and junk nails are also making noise with sleek, sculptural texture for the former and a maximalist approach to the latter with oversized charms, clashing textures and extreme customization.

Consumers are leaning into at-home expertise and expressive finishes. Gaoy and MelodySusie highlight a growing investment in DIY tools like gel kits, lamps and drills. Nail Labo caters to a rising demand for precision and minimalist artistry, drawing from Japanese nail culture that prioritizes clean lines, quality materials and technical skill. Caudalie introduces a skincare-forward angle with its hand and nailcare rooted in antioxidant-rich formulations. Meanwhile, Ethereal Lacquer is capturing attention through its holographic, metallic and multi-chrome polishes, signaling that many nail consumers are seeking and collecting bold, light-catching finishes that double as artistic self-expression.

The popularity of #OilToFoamCleanser reflects growing interest in innovative hybrid formats, suggesting consumers are drawn to easy and elevated routines. #OilySkinHack points to a problem-solving mindset, where users seek shareable solutions tailored to specific skin concerns, especially shine and congestion. Meanwhile, #ManiInspo and #GlitterHighlighter showcase visual beauty through inspiration and self-expression, with consumers looking for aesthetic ideas that feel fresh, playful and mood-driven. Lastly, #EdgeControlFor4cHair emphasizes the demand for texture-specific solutions and culturally resonant beauty techniques.

Matte powder is trending, as consumers seek polished, smooth and filtered‑like skin finishes. The popularity of pink lip stain and lipstick pencil, meanwhile, highlights a tilt toward bold lip looks that are still accessible and day‑to‑day friendly. Techniques like tightline eyeliner illustrate how subtle definition is gaining traction, reflecting a preference for minimal effort with big impact. Contrastingly, the surge in black lip stains suggest that consumers are also embracing more daring, identity‑driven looks that go beyond enhancement.

Among the top‑growing makeup brands, there’s an emphasis on accessible, niche aesthetics and cultural authenticity across price points. BBIA’s K‑beauty roots and affordable, vibrant product lines show how makeup lovers are drawn to colorful products that promote self-expression. Kulfi Beauty’s South Asian-inspired, inclusive shade range underscores a demand for brands that acknowledge and celebrate underrepresented skin tones and identities. On the other end of the pricing spectrum, Hermès brings luxury craftsmanship and premium finishes to makeup, signaling that consumers also view beauty as a status and lifestyle experience. Meanwhile, Palladio Beauty and UCoolMe illustrate how ingredient-driven products and purpose‑driven formats (like lash clusters) are becoming non‑negotiable for many buyers.

On beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer behavior shift toward accessibility, self‑expression and targeted problem‑solving. The surge in #EyelashLiftAndTint showcases how users are seeking out tutorial‑friendly content and at‑home techniques to achieve salon‑level transformations. Meanwhile, #BraidingExtensions and #NailsDesignIdeas point to a growing appetite for creative styling and personalization in hair and nails. At the same time, #KojicAndTurmericSoap highlights the fascination with viral, ingredient‑centric skincare that promises visible pay-off through ‘miracle’ formulas. Lastly, #PinkLipLiner reflects a subtle shift from cool-tone nudes toward warmer, reddish-pink tones that add soft color while still feeling natural — indicating consumers’ evolving preference for makeup that enhances without overpowering.

The rise of morning shed, the ritualized removal of multiple overnight beauty tools and treatments, highlights a growing fascination with stacked, intensive skincare routines that promise overnight results. Searches for face-lifting masks reflect a desire for visible tightening, while hydrogel’s jelly-like, cooling texture satisfies a craving for sensorial, soothing formats. Meanwhile, rising interest in milky toners and turmeric face creams shows demand for gentle nourishment and targeted actives, with turmeric specifically valued for its natural, hyperpigmentation-reducing benefits.

By brand, Grace & Stella and Byoma each represent a demand for approachable, feel-good skincare — whether through playful formats like eye masks or barrier-repair formulas that emphasize maintenance and simplicity. In contrast, brands like AnteAge, Bioeffect and Medik8 cater to a results-focused audience seeking science-led actives like EGF and retinal, signaling rising trust in clinical, regenerative skincare that targets aging and skin renewal at a deeper level. Consumers are embracing a dual approach to skincare, blending routine-friendly support with targeted, high-performance treatments, depending on need, mood, or life stage.

In the TikTok sphere, trending beauty hashtags are focusing on age inclusivity, professional-level prep, and tailored care for specific identities and beauty concerns. #BeautyOver60 spotlights content that speaks directly to mature audiences, as those aged 60-plus seek routines and products that speak to their evolving needs and celebrate aging confidently. #BridalSkinPrep, often used by makeup artists, reflects interest in expert-driven techniques that enhance makeup application, as consumers value the behind-the-scenes steps that create flawless, event-ready skin. Meanwhile, #CollegeHairstylist, #RedHaircare and #CeramideSerum point to highly specialized content — from on-campus hairstyling services to color-specific hair routines and barrier-supporting ingredients — illustrating a broader trend toward community-rooted expertise and ingredient-conscious skincare.

Haircare is of increasing importance to consumers, as beauty focuses go beyond the surface to tackle cosmetic concerns at their root. The rise of DHT blocker shampoos and scalp serums signal growing concern around hair thinning and scalp health, with consumers turning to targeted treatments that address hair loss at its source. Interest in lightweight conditioners and hair UV protection highlights desire for gentle hydration and environmental defense, which avoids build-up and leans into skincare. Hair fiber powders are also rising, especially among young males, as consumers seek quick-fix solutions to thinning and receding, issues becoming more prevalent in social dialogue.

Among haircare brands, there’s a consumer shift toward precision and wellness‑infused formulations. Cerave’s expansion into haircare underscores the demand for dermatologist‑approved, barrier‑support solutions — with ceramides and niacinamide anchoring formulas that consider scalp health as closely tied to hair health. Arey taps into a preventative and repigmentation‑focused niche by offering clinical systems to address greying hair, as more consumers seek anti‑aging hair solutions. Design Essentials and TGIN highlight a growing emphasis on texture‑specific haircare, delivering salon‑quality formulas for relaxed, natural and coily hair types. Meanwhile, Vichy brings its skin‑science heritage to hair with targeted treatments for dandruff.

On beauty TikTok, trending hashtags reflect a consumer shift toward efficiency, targeted solutions and hacks. The rise of #OnTheGoMakeup highlights how beauty routines are being compressed and adapted for busy lifestyles. #ChopstickCurls, referring to tight, defined curls achieved with ultra-thin rectangular-shaped wands, reflects consumer interest in niche, high-impact styling tools. Hashtags like #DepuffSkin, #OilySkinSolutions and #MicellarWaterHacks point to a demand for quick‑acting, problem‑solving formulas, especially those that tackle puffiness, oil control, or simplify skincare cleansing — reflecting an audience that wants visible change with minimal fuss.

In the evergrowing wellness space, consumers are leaning into metabolic health, enhanced performance and functional supplementation. The popularity of moringa supplements and probiotic shots reinforces interest in plant-based, gut-friendly solutions that offer antioxidant, digestive and anti-inflammatory benefits. As the links between gut health and other bodily concerns continue to emerge, consumers are turning to natural tools for internal balance and immunity support. Ketone and NAD supplements reveal that biohacking and longevity are still on consumers’ minds, as they seek ways to improve energy, cellular repair and cognitive performance through next-gen supplementation. Meanwhile, inferno Pilates lean into the high-intensity, hybrid fitness formats that combine strength with cardio — signaling a demand for wellness routines that challenge the body while delivering visible, fast-track results.

When it comes to wellness brands, Puori stands out for its ultra‑transparent, minimalist supplements that indicate a strong consumer demand for trustworthy quality and ingredient purity. Javy Coffee merges convenience and function by offering high‑protein, sugar‑free coffee concentrates, hinting that wellness is being woven into everyday routines as well as indulgent moments. Meanwhile, brands like VH Essentials focus on women’s intimate health with probiotic‑rich, lifestyle‑friendly formats, signaling a move towards specific wellness needs and gender‑tailored solutions. Lastly, Snap Supplements and Alaya Naturals emphasize science‑backed formulas, superfood blends and adaptogens, while highlighting how modern consumers are gravitating toward preventative, system‑focused wellness — gut, hormones, vitality — rather than generic multivitamins.

Fragrance notes like tonka bean, marshmallow and chocolate are doing the rounds this month, marking a shift towards gourmand scents that evoke warmth, nostalgia and emotional selfcare. The rise of skin perfume, specifically, suggests a desire for intimate, personal and subtle scent expression, via those that feel like an extension of one’s natural body rather than a bold statement. Overall, the convergence of edible sweetness and minimalist sensuality reflects a broader cultural movement towards self-soothing luxury and authenticity in beauty.

Interest in fragrance names like Penhaligon’s and Arquiste signals a craving for heritage, craftsmanship and historical storytelling, while brands like Fugazzi, Mind Games and Salt & Stone appeal to a modern, conceptual take on scent as identity and lifestyle. Together, they illustrate how consumers are moving beyond simple scent preference into fragrances that express intellect, emotion and personal storytelling. The blend of artisanal tradition with contemporary creativity underscores a desire for depth and meaning in luxury purchases.
